title: Patanjali — Depth & Specificity Research
content:
Patanjali Ayurved has expanded its product portfolio to include food products, natural health care, personal care, medicines, home care, apparels, and more. In June 2025, Patanjali announced a mega food park project in Vizianagaram district, Andhra Pradesh. The company also partnered with the Russian Government in December 2025 to promote health & wellness and tourism. Patanjali launched Swadeshi Samriddhi SIM cards in May 2018 in partnership with BSNL and opened a hospital in January 2026, inaugurated by India's home minister Amit Shah. Additionally, Patanjali has built a strong supply chain in its oil business, teaching farmers to increase yield and buying directly from them to cut out middlemen.

In June 2025, Patanjali announced a mega food park project on 172.84 acres in Vizianagaram district. Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (APIIC) had acquired ‘D' patta lands from farmers for the project.

In December 2025, Patanjali partnerred with Russian Government to promote health & wellness and tourism.

## Products

[edit] [...] [edit]

Patanjali Ayurved produces cosmetics and personal-care, ayurvedic and food products. The company opened Patanjali Paridhan, a clothing store in Delhi, in November 2018.

In May 2018, Patanjali launched Swadeshi Samriddhi SIM cards in partnership with BSNL.

## Revenue

[edit] [...] In 2025, Patanjali Ayurved along with DS Group acquired Magma General Insurance for ₹4,500 crore.

In December 2025, The Government of Tripura partnered with Patanjali Ayurved for a project in Tripura State worth Rs 300-400 crores.

Patanjali Ayurved opened a hospital "Patanjali Emergency & Critical Care Hospital" on 22nd January 2026 which was inaugurated by home minister of India Amit Shah.

Patanjali employs a penetrative pricing strategy, positioning its products 10-30% below comparable multinational offerings, according to multiple retail market analyses. This approach, noted in Business Standard and Mint during 2016-2017, made Patanjali accessible to price-sensitive Indian consumers while maintaining brand premiumization through quality claims and naturality positioning. Patanjali’s pricing model undercuts established players like HUL and Dabur by 15–20%, making it highly attractive to price-sensitive rural consumers, as noted by KPMG and Economic Times. Patanjali’s products are priced 20-30% lower than competitors, appealing to lower and middle-income groups.

Patanjali targets rural and semi-urban areas across India, focusing on consumers who prefer natural, herbal, and Ayurvedic products. The company leverages culturally relevant positioning, emphasizing Indian heritage and traditional remedies, which resonates strongly with rural consumers. Patanjali's marketing tactics include using regional languages and local festivals, and it has made a strategic priority of rural India, harnessing traditional health values, competitive pricing, and innovative distribution to reach millions of rural consumers. Additionally, Patanjali's penetrative pricing strategy, offering products 20-30% cheaper than competitors, appeals to lower and middle-income groups.
